body.p: Claim 1 has been amended to recite that the at least one particle is positioned in an optically interrogatable position with respect to light transmitted through the member to the end portion. Support for this amendment may be found in the specification, for example, on page 7, lines 21-26.
In addition, new dependent claims 135-141 have been added. Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, for example, on page 13, lines 27-29 or on page 19, lines 20-22.
Claims 1-3, 5, 30, 37, 42, 43, 47, and 135-141 are now pending for examination. Claims 50, 52, 55, 66, 67, 77, 83, 84, 91, 92, and 96 have been withdrawn. No new matter has been added.
Claims 1-3, 5, 30, 37, 42, 43, and 47 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by Rylander, et al., U.S. Pat. Apl. Pub. No. 2013/0338627 ("Rylander").

It is not seen where Rylander teaches or suggests at least one particle that is positioned in an optically interrogatable position with respect to light transmitted through the member to the end portion, as is recited in claim 1, as amended. As discussed in the specification, the at least one particle may be optically interrogated using light, e.g., using techniques such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR).
In contrast, such particles are not taught or suggested by Rylander. While Rylander does

suggest that particles may be present (see, e.g., paragraphs 0283, 0295, 0297, and 0303, as identified in the Office Action), the particles in Rylander are intended to be delivered into the tissue (paragraph 0283), and once delivered, the particles used to induce selective photothermal or photochemical damage to the target tissue (paragraph 0295). Thus, Rylander actually teaches away from at least one particle immobilized relative to the end portion of the member, as recited in claim 1, as particles that were so immobilized would not be delivered into the tissue, which would cause Rylander to fail in its intended use. Nowhere does Rylander teach or suggest that such particles are intended to be optically interrogated, rather than being delivered into the tissue (e.g., into a tumor) within a subject.
Accordingly, for at least these reasons, it is believed that claim 1, as amended, is not
anticipated or rendered obvious by Rylander, and it is thus respectfully requested that the rejection
of claims 1-3, 5, 30, 37, 42, 43, and 47 as being anticipated by Rylander be withdrawn. It is also not conceded that the claims as pending prior to amendment herein were anticipated by Rylander.

In view of the foregoing remarks, this application should now be in condition for allowance. A notice to this effect is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes, after the foregoing remarks, that the application is not in condition for allowance, the Examiner is requested to call the undersigned at 617-646-8000.

If this response is not considered timely filed and if a suitable request for an extension of time is otherwise absent, any necessary extension of time is hereby requested.
